sanity_expectations: Itrans > 0 and finite/real everywhere in the sampled region

Near x=0 the beam is least attenuated (transmitted ≈ incident modulated by bleaching factor); attenuation grows with depth
Bounded above by roughly I0 near x=0
excitation_report: σ=0.03, k=5, Sobol over x∈[0,5], I0∈[0.5,10]. Term multiples of σ: main saturable/bleaching product term RMS 1.79 → 59.8×σ; additive scattering floor beta_scatter*(1-exp(-sigma_scatter*x)) RMS 0.19 → 6.4×σ. NEW term (two-photon absorption factor exp(-alpha_tpa*I0*exp(-alpha*x)*x/(1+I0*exp(-alpha*x)/Isat))): peak effect 0.93 → 31.0×σ, strongest near x≈0.87, I0≈5.87 (moderate depth, high intensity). I0: V->V (confirmed independent — incident intensity / power-sweep axis, excites intensity-dependent terms)
alpha: V->P (overridden: labeled input but is a fixed small-signal absorption coefficient of the medium; fixed to 1.0)
Isat: P->P (confirmed, fixed 1.0 as intensity normalization)
alpha_tpa: P->P (confirmed; coefficient of the NEW two-photon term, fixed 0.5 within suggested 0.0–2.0)
rationale: Static explicit Beer–Lambert-type relation with saturable absorption, thermal-repopulation bleaching (tanh), an additive multiple-scattering floor, and a NEW multiplicative two-photon-absorption factor. No derivatives/integrals → evaluate_explicit. x (thickness) is the primary axis and I0 (incident intensity) is a second axis so the intensity-dependent saturation/bleaching/TPA physics is identifiable; alpha is a fixed material constant, all others fixed. auto_balance tuned beta_scatter to make the scattering floor visible; excitation_check confirms every term including the new TPA factor exceeds 5σ within physical bounds (alpha_tpa=0.5 in the suggested 0–2 range).

scenario_text: A monochromatic electromagnetic wave passes through a slab of absorbing material, and its intensity diminishes with penetration depth. Each layer removes a fraction of the transmitted power proportional to the local intensity. We measure the transmitted intensity as a function of the slab thickness. The absorption coefficient of the medium sets the attenuation scale.
